cs.t: I became interested in Seiko watches after recently buying a Seiko Astron while visiting Japan. It’s amazing how much they shaped the watch industry. With the Astron series they buried a lot of Swiss manufacturers when it was first launched. Also, their “Spring Drive” technology is amazing. It’s basically the perfect hybrid between a mechanical watch movement and a quartz crystal. The movement is mechanical, with the spring releasing energy and powering the quartz crystal (there is no battery), which in turn acts as a “referee”, applying an electromagnetic brake and regulating the mechanical movement.
cs.th: The first watch featuring computer functions

cs.t: I settled on a Seiko Astron GPS Solar on my last Japan trip and am very happy. It is missing the number 3 and 5 as it is not a smart/connected watch but its tech excites me every time I think about it. So if you’re willing to sacrifice or want to have an alternative watch to your smart watch, I highly recommend looking into it.
For that you want a Seiko Astron GPS watch:  https://www.seikowatches.com/us-en/products/astron  (two decades ago it could have been a Timex Perpetual, but that's 404 these days)
